newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian metals' gain ahead of one-day strike.
newsitem.headline: Indian metals' gain ahead of one-day strike.

text.p: Indian copper, tin and nickel gained on Wednesday ahead of a one-day protest over rising tax rates, dealers said.
"Renewed industrial buying dragged prices up while supplies of imported metals remained low," one dealer said.

Ready copper rose by 50 rupees to 12,500 rupees per quintal and tin rose by 100 rupees to 34,500 rupees. Nickel was up by 300 rupees to 36,800 rupees. On Tuesday copper, tin and nickel were up by 50 rupees, 100 rupees and 300 rupees respectively.
Aluminium was quiet at 7,200 rupees per quintal, zinc at 6,500 rupees and lead at 4,400 rupees.
The Bombay Metal Exchange will be shut on Thursday to support a strike by traders protesting against a tax hike.
The markets will reopen on Friday.
